--- title: "October 18–22, 2026" date: 2026-10-18 description: "Network median 2.24 in (range 1.18–3.62 in); peak IVT 412 kg m⁻¹ s⁻¹ from the SSW" categories: [IVT ≥ 250, Snow, Final] execute: freeze: auto --- ## Summary Most of the rain fell between Wednesday morning, October 21, and Thursday morning, October 22, over about 29 hours. Rain gauges across Flagstaff caught a typical 2.24 inches, from 1.18 in at Spruce Wash at Route 66 to 3.62 in at Waterline Rd #1 (Lenox-Wupatki Trails). The airport measured 1.84 in, about 8 times the normal for those 5 days. Snow fell only at the highest mountain sites; in town it was rain. Nights were mild for the season, about 10 °F above normal. The storm was fed by an atmospheric river, a long, narrow stream of moist air flowing from the south-southwest, drawn north by an area of low pressure aloft centred about 830 miles to the west. 98% of the rain fell while that stream was overhead. All 18 USGS gauges within 68 miles had daily flows above the 90th percentile for the date. The Little Colorado River near Cameron peaked at 18,000 cubic feet per second (cfs), about 3 times its typical yearly peak (the median of annual peaks); West Clear Creek near Camp Verde peaked at 8,660 cfs, 2.6 times its typical yearly peak; Wet Beaver Creek near Rimrock peaked at 5,350 cfs, 2.1 times its typical yearly peak. Closer to town, Switzer Wash rose 1.9 ft, its highest since July 2021; Sinclair Wash near University Heights rose 2.3 ft, its highest since July 2021. (River flows are provisional.) ::: {.callout-note collapse="true"} ## Technical summary Across 37 gauges the event total ranged from 1.18 to 3.62 in (median 2.24 in). The central 80% of the network-mean rain fell between Oct 21 05:00 MST and Oct 22 10:00 MST (29 h). Moisture transport over Flagstaff reached atmospheric-river strength: ERA5 IVT was at or above 250 kg m⁻¹ s⁻¹ for 42 h and peaked at 412 kg m⁻¹ s⁻¹ from the SSW at Oct 21 11:00 MST. 98% of the network-mean rain fell while IVT was at or above 250. At the IVT peak, 500-hPa flow over Flagstaff was from the SSW at 28 m s⁻¹, and the 500-hPa trough axis along 35.25°N was at 126.2°W, 1,325 km west of Flagstaff (5,586 m, against 5,842 m over Flagstaff). A closed 500-hPa low (5,570 m) was centred 1,342 km to the W, at 34.0°N 126.2°W. The strongest 250-hPa wind within 1,000 km was 60 m s⁻¹, 731 km to the W. The 250-hPa wind over Flagstaff peaked at 43 m s⁻¹ (Oct 20 23:00 MST), 12 h before the IVT peak. ::: ## Rain across the network ::: {#50be6e76 .cell execution_count=3} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Event rain total at each city and county gauge (circle color and label show the total in inches; map cropped to the network) over shaded relief (USGS 3DEP), 200-m elevation contours, streams (USGS NHD) and highways (Census TIGER). Tap or click the map to open the frame full size.* ## What the forecasters said The National Weather Service office in Flagstaff discussed the moisture source in its Area Forecast Discussions as the event unfolded. Excerpts, quoted verbatim (links to the Iowa Environmental Mesonet archive): - **Oct 18, 2:03 AM MST** ([AFD](https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=AFDFGZ&e=202610180903)): "A southerly moisture surge is currently underway, somewhat enhanced by continued active tropical cyclone activity in the Eastern Pacific." - **Oct 19, 12:40 PM MST** ([AFD](https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=AFDFGZ&e=202610191940)): "On Wednesday and Thursday, the West Coast low shifts eastward toward northern Arizona allowing deep subtropical moisture to push into the area from the south. Some of this incoming moisture will be assocaited with what is currently Tropical Storm Trudy centered south of the Baja Peninsula." - **Oct 20, 2:47 PM MST** ([AFD](https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=AFDFGZ&e=202610202147)): "Some of this moisture is left over from post-tropical cyclone Trudy and is enhanced by the continued active tropical activity in the eastern Pacific." - **Oct 22, 3:00 AM MST** ([AFD](https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=AFDFGZ&e=202610221000)): "This system is pulling a rich subtropical moisture plume into the state, yielding record amounts of atmospheric moisture for this time of year." ## Climate context - **Airport precipitation:** 1.84 in over 5 local days, against a 1991–2020 normal of 0.24 in for those days (8× normal). - **Rank:** the 31st largest 5-day airport total in October among 129 years with data since 1898 (each year's largest 5-day total ending in October). - **Airport temperature:** highs averaged -2.0 °F and lows +10.2 °F relative to normal. - **Water year to date** (Oct 1, 2026 – Oct 22, 2026): airport 5.39 in (normal 1.08 in);
